sourcedFrom: P99 AS P99 QA P99 DAO Full Size/Compact — Instruction Manual CDN GB — Rev. f (UNKNOWN — no copyright line printed; the part number dates the printing to 06-2010)
cleanIntro: The P99 AS is the Anti-Stress trigger version — striker-fired, but with a decocker in the top of the slide and a genuine double-action first shot. That decocker is not a convenience here: the pistol physically cannot be field stripped until the striker is decocked with it. This book covers the AS alongside the QA and the DAO, in Full Size and Compact frames, and it splits by variant repeatedly, so read the headings. It publishes striker, extractor and magazine disassembly, so there is a real deep procedure.

steps.title: Establish that it is an AS, and which frame
steps.action: Look at the top rear of the slide. A P99 AS has a decocker button there; a P99 QA has a field-stripping aid in the same place; a P99 DAO has neither. Then note whether the frame is Full Size or Compact — that changes the recoil rod orientation on reassembly.
steps.prose: This one book covers three different trigger mechanisms and the procedures diverge, so getting the variant wrong means following instructions for a gun you do not own. The AS is the one with a working decocker used routinely after loading and before holstering; the QA's identical-looking button is a field-stripping aid that leaves the pistol not ready for service once pressed. The frame question is separate and equally real — Full Size and Compact take the recoil guide rod assembly in opposite orientations. Settle both now, with the pistol empty.
steps.aside: A Full Size magazine can be used in a P99 Compact only with the proper adapter. Walther's caution: use the adapter, to avoid damage to the ejector.
steps.quote: P99 AS P99 QA P99 DAO Full Size/Compact
steps.cite: P99 AS P99 QA P99 DAO Full Size/Compact — Instruction Manual CDN GB — Rev. f — Cover, PDF p.1

steps.title: Magazine out, using the trigger-guard release
steps.action: Finger straight and outside the guard, muzzle in a safe direction. Press the ambidextrous magazine release at the trigger guard — thumb or opposing index finger — and remove the magazine from the pistol.
steps.prose: The P99's release is a paddle at the trigger guard rather than a button on the grip, so it works from either side and is easy to reach without breaking the firing grip. If your shooting thumb finds it awkward, Walther's own suggestion is the index finger of the shooting hand. Take the magazine right out and put it away from the bench: what follows ends in a trigger press. On a Compact fitted with a Full Size magazine and adapter, remember that the adapter comes with the magazine.
steps.quote: Grasp the pistol with your finger off the trigger and outside the trigger guard. Depress the magazine release and remove the magazine.
steps.cite: P99 AS P99 QA P99 DAO Full Size/Compact — Instruction Manual CDN GB — Rev. f — 2.6.3 Magazine Release, printed p.7 (PDF p.7)

steps.title: Rack hard, lock open, check chamber and bore
steps.action: Grip the rear slide serrations, draw the slide fully rearward in one brisk stroke to extract and clear any chambered round, lock it open by easing it slightly forward while pressing up on the slide stop, then verify the chamber is empty and the bore is clear.
steps.prose: Do not obstruct the ejection port with the supporting hand as you rack — a blocked port drops the round back into the action instead of throwing it clear. With the slide locked open you can see into the chamber and straight down the magazine well, and the P99's frame gives a good view of both. Check the bore while you have the line of sight; an obstruction found now costs nothing and one found later costs the barrel. Walther requires this whole sequence every time the pistol leaves your hand.
steps.quote: Lock the slide in the open position by allowing the slide to move slightly forward from the rearmost position while pressing upward on the slide stop (3.1 Fig. 3).
steps.cite: P99 AS P99 QA P99 DAO Full Size/Compact — Instruction Manual CDN GB — Rev. f — 3.1 Inspecting the Pistol, printed p.9 (PDF p.9)
steps.warn: You must follow this procedure every time the P99 leaves your hand, is cleaned, handed to you or another person, transported or stored.

steps.title: Read the striker status indicator by feel, not by eye alone
steps.action: Look and feel at the rear of the slide. On a cocked P99 the striker tip protrudes from the slide end cap. In the de-cocked state it can be neither seen nor felt. Confirm by touch.
steps.prose: This is the P99's most useful feature at the bench and the one most owners never use: the striker itself is the indicator, protruding through the end cap when cocked. Because it is a physical protrusion it can be read in the dark, in a holster, or with cold hands, which is more than any painted marking offers. It is also how you will confirm the decocker did its job before you attempt the take-down catch. Note that on a P99 QA the ready-for-service state leaves the tip about 1 mm inside the cap — visible but not feelable — which is not the AS behaviour.
steps.aside: The P99 has a cocking indicator in the rear of the slide, using the internal striker's own tip. There is no separate part to break or lose.
steps.quote: In the de-cocked state, the tip can be neither seen nor felt (2.6 Fig. 2, left side).
steps.cite: P99 AS P99 QA P99 DAO Full Size/Compact — Instruction Manual CDN GB — Rev. f — 2.6.2 Striker Status Indicator, printed p.7 (PDF p.7)

steps.title: Decock the striker — the AS will not strip until you do
steps.action: With the muzzle pointed in a safe direction, close the slide and press the decocker downwards into the slide until the striker is audibly and visually de-cocked. Confirm at the rear of the slide that the striker tip no longer protrudes.
steps.prose: This is the step that makes a P99 AS different from every other striker pistol on the bench: the take-down catch is mechanically blocked while the striker is cocked, and no amount of pressing will free it. The decocker is the routine control on this pistol — used after loading, before holstering, and before disassembly — so the motion should already be familiar. Point the pistol in a safe direction while you do it, every time, because you are releasing a striker. And note the trap that follows: pulling the slide rearward at any point after this re-cocks it, and you will have to decock again.
steps.quote: The P99 AS and P99 QA can be fieldstripped only when the striker is decocked: De-cock the pistol by depressing the decocker (P99 AS) or field-stripping aid (P99 QA).
steps.cite: P99 AS P99 QA P99 DAO Full Size/Compact — Instruction Manual CDN GB — Rev. f — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.14 (PDF p.14)
steps.warn: Pulling the slide rearward will cock the striker again. A P99 DAO has neither a decocker nor a field-stripping aid and does not take this step at all.

steps.title: Take-down catch down both sides, slide off the front
steps.action: Grip the take-down catch from above with a finger each side and press it straight downwards. Hold it there and move the slide forward off the frame.
steps.prose: Both sides must go down together — a one-sided squeeze cants the catch in its slot and it will not release, which on a decocked P99 is the usual reason someone concludes the pistol is broken. Come from above so your hand stays behind the muzzle as the slide travels. If the catch refuses even with both sides loaded evenly, go back and check the striker indicator: an AS that has been racked since decocking is cocked again. Once the catch drops the slide comes off with no resistance, so support it.
steps.quote: Grip the take down catch from above on both sides and press downwards (4.1 Fig. 1).
steps.cite: P99 AS P99 QA P99 DAO Full Size/Compact — Instruction Manual CDN GB — Rev. f — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.14 (PDF p.14)

steps.title: Recoil assembly out, then the barrel
steps.action: Invert the slide, lift the recoil guide rod assembly out from below the barrel while taking up the spring pressure, then lift the barrel out of the slide.
steps.prose: The assembly is captive but loaded; ease the end out of the barrel recess rather than pulling, or it will spring out of your fingers. The barrel then lifts free. That is the whole P99 field strip and the manual's own figure shows the four components — frame, slide, barrel, recoil guide rod assembly — so lay them against it. On a Full Size 9mm it is normal for the recoil guide rod to protrude very slightly from the slide once reassembled; the manual says so, and it is not a sign of a wrong part.
steps.aside: It is normal for the recoil guide rod to slightly protrude from the Full Size 9mm slide.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil guide rod assembly from below the barrel while taking up the spring pressure (4.1 Fig. 2).
steps.cite: P99 AS P99 QA P99 DAO Full Size/Compact — Instruction Manual CDN GB — Rev. f — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.14 (PDF p.14)

steps.title: Full Size and Compact take the recoil rod in OPPOSITE orientations
steps.action: Note before reassembly which frame you have. On a P99 Full Size the SMALLER black end of the recoil rod goes into the spring mounting at the front of the slide, with the large polymer end into the lower barrel recess. On a P99 Compact it is the LARGE spring end that goes into the front mounting.
steps.prose: This is the reassembly error that produces a P99 which will not go back together, and the reason people force parts that should slide. On a Compact there is an additional step before it will seat at all: align the front end of the large recoil spring so it is centred on the polymer front end of the recoil rod, which the manual illustrates as proper versus improper alignment. Get that centring wrong and the assembly binds no matter which end you present. Read the frame, not your memory of the last P99 you handled.
steps.quote: P99 Full Size: Place the smaller (black) end of the recoil rod into the spring mounting at the front of the slide, and then insert the large polymer end of the recoil spring into the lower barrel recess, while taking up the spring pressure
steps.cite: P99 AS P99 QA P99 DAO Full Size/Compact — Instruction Manual CDN GB — Rev. f — 4.1.2 Field-Stripping Reassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.15)
steps.warn: P99 Full Size and P99 Compact are not interchangeable here. A Compact also needs the large spring centred on the rod's polymer front end before it will seat.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel, recoil guide rod assembly. That is the published P99 field strip — the striker assembly, the extractor and the magazine belong to the deeper procedure.
steps.prose: Lay the four out against the main-components figure before any solvent is opened. The routine clean from here reaches the bore from the chamber end, the breech face, the chamber end of the barrel, the extractor and its surroundings, and the frame. Note that on reassembly a P99 AS gets one extra action nobody else does: once the slide is back on and forward, the striker is decocked again with the decocker pressed all the way down. If you want the slide internals out, that is the deep procedure and it needs a 2 mm punch.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel from the slide.
steps.cite: P99 AS P99 QA P99 DAO Full Size/Compact — Instruction Manual CDN GB — Rev. f — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.14 (PDF p.14)

deepSteps.title: Slide end cap off with a 2 mm punch
deepSteps.action: Field strip the pistol, then stand the muzzle end of the slide on a smooth flat surface. Grip it at the slide serrations, push the pin in through the square opening at the top right of the slide end cap with a 2 mm punch, and slide the end cap downwards out of the slide.
deepSteps.prose: The cap is holding the striker spring, so keep a thumb across it as the pin releases — this is where a striker assembly goes across the room. Standing the slide on its muzzle keeps everything travelling towards you. The opening is square and offset to the right of the cap; probing another hole with a punch damages the parts behind it. Use a proper 2 mm punch rather than an improvised drift, because the pin face is small and a slipped punch marks the slide.
deepSteps.quote: Field-strip the pistol. Place the muzzle end of the slide on a smooth, flat surface.
deepSteps.cite: P99 AS P99 QA P99 DAO Full Size/Compact — Instruction Manual CDN GB — Rev. f — 4.2.1 Remove Striker Assembly, printed p.16 (PDF p.16)
deepSteps.warn: The striker assembly is under spring pressure behind the end cap. Control it as the cap clears.

deepSteps.title: On an AS, the striker releases the DECOCKER — cover it
deepSteps.action: As you draw the striker assembly out of the slide, cover the decocker with a finger. On a P99 AS or QA, removing the striker assembly releases the decocker or field-stripping aid; take the striker out first, then lift the decocker out.
deepSteps.prose: This is the AS-specific trap in the deep strip, and it is the reason the manual splits this instruction by variant. The decocker is retained by the striker assembly, so the moment the striker leaves, the decocker is free to fall out of the top of the slide — usually onto the floor, where a small polymer button is hard to find. A P99 DAO behaves differently again: on that gun it is the drop safety that is released, in two parts. Know which you have before the striker moves.
deepSteps.quote: Cover the decocker/field-stripping aid while you remove the striker assembly, then remove the decocker/field-stripping aid.
deepSteps.cite: P99 AS P99 QA P99 DAO Full Size/Compact — Instruction Manual CDN GB — Rev. f — 4.2.1 Remove Striker Assembly, P99 AS and P99 QA, printed p.16 (PDF p.16)

deepSteps.title: Extractor: control the striker safety and the plunger
deepSteps.action: Place the slide upside down with the muzzle facing to the left. Push the extractor plunger in with a 2 mm punch, cover the striker safety and the extractor plunger with a finger, and pivot the extractor out. Remove the striker safety assembly and the extractor plunger assembly.
deepSteps.prose: Two sprung parts come free at once here and both will leave the slide if your finger lifts — that is exactly what the manual's warning covers. Push the plunger in first, then get the covering finger in place before the extractor pivots. Pivot the rear end out slowly rather than levering it against the slide. Lay the striker safety assembly and the extractor plunger assembly out in the order they came, because reassembly runs in reverse and the small springs are easy to swap.
deepSteps.quote: Place the slide upside down with the muzzle facing to the left. Push in the extractor plunger with a 2 mm punch (4.3 Fig. 1).
deepSteps.cite: P99 AS P99 QA P99 DAO Full Size/Compact — Instruction Manual CDN GB — Rev. f — 4.3.1 Remove Extractor, printed p.17 (PDF p.17)
deepSteps.warn: While you remove the extractor, be sure to control the striker safety and the extractor plunger so that they do not fly out.

deepSteps.title: Extractor back in — plunger holds itself, then snaps home
deepSteps.action: Slide upside down, muzzle to the left. Insert the striker safety assembly and the extractor plunger assembly. Align the extractor's rear end to its slot, press it towards the slide with your thumb, push the extractor plunger down with the 2 mm punch and press the extractor in until they hold each other. Withdraw the punch, then press the extractor fully in until the plunger snaps into its hole.
deepSteps.prose: The trick is the intermediate state: you press the extractor in only far enough that the eyelet of the extractor holds down the extractor plunger, which frees your punch hand. Push it fully home before that point and the plunger jumps. Once the punch is out, hold the safety plunger flush with the slide surface and press the extractor the rest of the way; the snap is audible and is your confirmation. If there is no snap, the plunger has not found its hole and the extractor is only friction-held.
deepSteps.quote: Hold the safety plunger down flush with the surface of the slide. Press in the extractor completely until the plunger snaps into the hole of the extractor (4.3 Fig. 4).
deepSteps.cite: P99 AS P99 QA P99 DAO Full Size/Compact — Instruction Manual CDN GB — Rev. f — 4.3.2 Install Extractor, printed p.17 (PDF p.17)

deepSteps.title: Striker back in, decocker first on an AS
deepSteps.action: On a P99 AS, insert the decocker from the top of the slide and depress it just enough to sit flush with the slide surface while you insert the striker assembly from the rear. Then press the striker assembly in with the slide end cap and reinsert the cap from the bottom of the slide until it snaps into place.
deepSteps.prose: The decocker must be held flush or the striker assembly will not pass under it — this is the mirror image of the removal step and it is the point where an AS reassembly stalls. Hold it down with a fingertip rather than a tool so you can feel when the striker clears. The end cap is what presses the assembly home against the spring, so use it as the tool rather than trying to push the striker in by hand. The snap at the bottom of the slide is the confirmation.
deepSteps.quote: Insert the decocker/field-stripping aid from the top of the slide and depress it just enough so that it is flush with the surface of the slide while inserting the striker assembly from the rear.
deepSteps.cite: P99 AS P99 QA P99 DAO Full Size/Compact — Instruction Manual CDN GB — Rev. f — 4.2.2 Install Striker Assembly, P99 AS and P99 QA, printed p.16 (PDF p.16)

deepSteps.title: Magazine down to its parts
deepSteps.action: Depress the floorplate catch through the hole in the floorplate with a 4 mm punch, slide the floorplate forward off the tube while keeping the catch pressed, take the catch and spring out through the bottom, then turn the tube right side up and remove the follower.
deepSteps.prose: Keep a thumb across the floorplate as it slides — the catch is the only thing restraining the spring and it will go across the room otherwise. Wear safety glasses; the manual asks for them specifically on magazine work. Everything comes out through the bottom of the tube, and everything goes back in exactly the orientation it came out. If a Compact magazine has an adapter fitted, take that off first and keep it with the magazine.
deepSteps.quote: Using a 4 mm punch, depress the floorplate catch through the hole in the floorplate (4.4 Fig. 1).
deepSteps.cite: P99 AS P99 QA P99 DAO Full Size/Compact — Instruction Manual CDN GB — Rev. f — 4.4.1 Magazine Disassembly, printed p.17 (PDF p.17)
deepSteps.warn: The magazine spring is under pressure. Control the floorplate catch and the spring while you remove the floorplate.

deepSteps.title: Decock again once the pistol is back together
deepSteps.action: After the slide is on the frame and running fully forward into the locked position, press the decocker all the way down to de-cock the striker.
deepSteps.prose: Reassembling the slide cocks the striker, so a P99 AS that is put back together and set down is a cocked pistol with a single-action trigger — which is precisely what the decocker exists to prevent. This is the last action of the strip, not an afterthought, and Walther prints it as its own bullet in the reassembly sequence. Confirm it worked at the rear of the slide: the striker tip should be neither visible nor feelable. Then run the function check.
deepSteps.quote: P99 AS only: De-cock the striker by pressing the decocker all the way down.
deepSteps.cite: P99 AS P99 QA P99 DAO Full Size/Compact — Instruction Manual CDN GB — Rev. f — 4.1.2 Field-Stripping Reassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.15)

cleaning.name: BARREL & CHAMBER
tasks: Brush from the CHAMBER end until the bristles fully exit at the muzzle, then pull back until they fully exit at the chamber end — never reverse the brush inside the bore
Powder-removing solvent and a brass bristle bore brush to lift lead and firing residue out of the six-groove bore
Wipe out with patches or a swab, then a light film of gun lubricant on the barrel's external surfaces and on the ramp where the locking block cams the barrel
Wipe all excess oil and preservative out of the bore and chamber before firing

cleaning.name: SLIDE, BREECH FACE & EXTRACTOR
tasks: Small brush in solvent around the breech face, the chamber end of the barrel, the extractor and all adjacent areas exposed to powder or primer residue
Clean around the decocker's seat at the top rear of the slide — grit there is what makes an AS decocker feel gritty or stiff
One drop of lubricant on the striker and one on the safety plunger
Confirm the striker status indicator still moves freely — it is the pistol's cocked/decocked read-out

cleaning.name: FRAME & RAILS
tasks: Light brushing with solvent to lift residue off the frame
A light coat of gun lubricant on the mechanism; one drop on the slide guides and one on the trigger bar
Light film of high quality gun lubricant on all external metal surfaces, then wipe clean
Cold climate: use a lubricant that will not congeal at low temperature

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Light film of gun lubricant on external metal surfaces only; wipe the tube interior dry
Inspect the feed lips and follower while the magazine is apart; never use excessive force reassembling it
Compact owners using Full Size magazines: clean and refit the adapter — Walther requires it to avoid damage to the ejector
Safety glasses on for any magazine assembly or disassembly

cleaning.name: SOLVENT LIMITS
tasks: No ammonia-based or strong alkaline solvents on any Walther firearm
Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning
Never manipulate, adjust or change internal components beyond what this procedure covers

reassembly: Slide upside down, barrel in with the locking lugs oriented as the manual's figure shows.

P99 Full Size: smaller black end of the recoil rod into the front spring mounting, large polymer end of the spring into the lower barrel recess. P99 Compact: centre the large spring on the rod's polymer front end first, then the large spring end goes into the front mounting.
Flex in the recoil guide rod assembly as it seats is normal; on a Full Size 9mm slight protrusion of the rod is also normal.
Push the slide onto the frame from the front until the take-down catch engages, making sure it also engages the REAR slide guides, then release it fully forward into the locked position.
P99 AS: press the decocker all the way down to de-cock the striker. Confirm at the rear of the slide that the tip is neither visible nor feelable.
Magazine: follower, spring and floorplate catch back in their original orientation, floorplate slid on until the catch snaps audibly into its hole.
Dry-patch the bore before the pistol is loaded or holstered.
fncheck: Magazine out and chamber confirmed empty: rack the slide and let it go — it must run fully into battery unaided. Lock it open on the slide stop and release it with the thumb. Insert the empty magazine and pull down on the floorplate; it must not move. Now the AS-specific checks: with the striker cocked (tip protruding at the rear of the slide) the take-down catch must refuse to depress; press the decocker and the tip should disappear both to the eye and to the finger, and the catch should then go down. Dry-fire once from decocked and the first press should be the long double-action stroke, with subsequent presses short and single-action until the decocker is used again. Finally check the extractor sits flush and springs back, and leave the pistol decocked.
